raw_response:
**My thinking:**

I've been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life. My two sons left for Handan years ago — it's just me and my wife now, working about 10 mu. I'm not going to try anything new at 65. Wheat and corn is what I know. The soil here, the groundwater, the market — it all suits wheat-corn rotation. I've done it forty years.

For wheat, I already put the seed in last October. Right now I'm watching it green up. I use the improved variety from the county seed shop — not the old traditional ones my father grew. The yields are better and everyone around here uses them now. I'll pump water four times: I already did the winter irrigation before freeze, and I'll irrigate again at green-up, jointing, and heading. I don't want to risk a dry spell ruining the grain fill.

For fertilizer I apply compound fertilizer as base before planting, then I top-dress with urea in spring. I probably put on a bit more than I need — I know that — but I'd rather have a good harvest than save a few yuan on fertilizer and watch the crop suffer.

After wheat comes off in June, I'll plant corn the same week. Hybrid seed, same as always. Corn doesn't need as many waterings if the rains come, but I'll pump twice to be safe. Corn borer has been bad some years, so I'll spray once.

I hire a rotary tiller from the village for both crops. My back can't handle plowing myself anymore.
